market.conclusion: Tech is in a downtrend: QQQ is below both its 50-day and 200-day averages. The broad market is sideways, and fear is elevated at a VIX of 22.91. Only 18% of stocks are above their 50-day average, and money is moving to defensive sectors such as staples (XLP +8.99) while tech lags (XLK -7.2). This is a reason for patience on new swing trades, but not for panic: credit shows no stress.
arguments: Macro (tech downtrend, fear elevated): I weigh this heavily. It is the one view that applies to every name, and breadth confirms it.
Technical (most charts in downtrends or ranges below their 50-day average): I weigh this heavily for swing calls. Not one name has a clean uptrend.
Fundamental (NVDA, NFLX and ORCL are good businesses at or below fair value): this decides the long-term verdicts, but it does not tell us when the selling stops.
Credit (spreads steady at 3.34, 'no stress in lending'): this argues for a correction in tech, not a broad crisis. That is why long-term buying in stages still makes sense.
Quant (no validated evidence; 0 of 413 forecasts scored): I give this no weight in either direction.
market.change_mind: A close above $663.84 on QQQ and above $739.76 on SPY would make me look for Enter setups. Widening credit spreads, or a bad reaction to NVDA's results, would make me more cautious. The 2026-11-25 GDP and PCE inflation releases are the next macro test.

deep_dive.case_for: It is a grade A business with sales up 83.38% over the past year. It is priced at $155.46, below its whole value range of $189.87–$411.04, and in the bottom 3.57% of its own 5-year price-to-sales range. The forward P/E is 9.73, and an RSI of 22.5 means it is oversold.
deep_dive.case_against: The chart is in a downtrend after a -28.18% month. The operating margin of 65% is at the top of its 5-year range, and peaks like that usually fade. Unpaid customer bills rose 127% while sales rose 106%. Insiders sold $946.6M outside pre-set plans. A headline also says this is the first report since Jensen Huang's exit.
deep_dive.decides: The market's reaction to the results released after today's close. A close that holds above $147.59 and later clears $169.14 would confirm that buyers are back. A close below $147.59 means the long-term buy should be built even more slowly.
